title: Expand Astro into an industrial yard with controllable MÖRK
context: The owner reported roughly 50 FPS and requested robotic assembly, logistics/cargo, solar power, an open reactor, connecting Fortification foundations and free-camera/tank-control modes on keys 1 and 3.
outcome: Five additional intact GLBs are pinned at upstream b22a8c9a6e04d40819b68859624f362d6bff8680. The yard adds the assembly cycle, cargo bay, solar complex with preserved tracking hinges and open reactor, connected by a non-overlapping lattice of instanced 4 m foundation tiles. Static material batching reduces solar to 45 batches, cargo to 8 and reactor to 7 while preserving assembly animation (333 batches). Foundations share five material batches. All groups have performance/visibility controls. Key 1 restores the free orbit camera and parks the tank; key 3 enables a chase camera, WASD/arrows, reverse/braking, wheel zoom and on-screen driving buttons. The tank faces the station on entry. Mode switches, focus loss and deactivation clear held controls. Motion uses the shared MÖRK feel adapter; a pure flat-yard drive module supplies conservative structure collisions without modifying game balance or construction/power/logistics rules.
alternatives: Batch stationary geometry under articulation owners rather than importing a second renderer or flattening animated machinery.
A shared foundation tile lattice avoids overlapping half-cell intersections; the authored foundation top remains the road surface.
The initial drive view faced away from the station because the scale-study tank faced the free camera. Its initial yard heading now points into the site.
evidence: npm run check and npm run build passed; new pinned assets validated
npm run test:browser: full source suite passed

node scripts/browser-test.mjs --dist --astro passed: industry assets, foundation counts, solar batching, key 3 movement/steering/lift, key 1 driving exclusion, typing isolation, animation and performance controls, shared settings and disposal
